acceptance: With the base commit available in the reviewer workspace, a `git diff` counts as a read of a file only with an explicit revision range against the base (for example `git diff <base>..HEAD -- path`), and `git show <base>:path` is not counted as a read of the head file. A bare `git diff -- path` on the clean head checkout and `git show HEAD -- path` do not count.
Count, quiet and file-name-only flags (`grep -l`, `grep -c`, `rg -q`), and zero-length head/tail (`head -n 0`), do not count
Each excluded form is a test case in tests/unit/scripts/oracle_reviewers/test_evidence.py

description: evidence.reads_file counts any content-reading command with the file as an operand. Several of these print nothing of the head version: `git diff -- path` on the clean head checkout, `git show <base>:path`, `git show HEAD -- path`, `head -n 0`, `grep -l/-c` and `rg -q`. The check is a tripwire for reviewers that read nothing, but a reviewer can satisfy it without seeing the changed code. A Read or Grep naming the file counts by design (decision record, _project/decisions/oracle-review-protocol-2026-10-08.md:47), so that is out of scope. Deferred from #2783 (Medium, and a Low in its review body). The base-ref rules (`git show <base>:path`, ranged `git diff`) need the base commit in the reviewer workspace, which is tracked in oracle-reviewer-checkout-has-no-base-commit-20261009.
